newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP holds back reserve money goal release.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP holds back reserve money goal release.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland will not publish its reserve money target for this month because the lower house of parliament has not yet passed the central bank's 1997 monetary policy outline, a senior NBP official said.

"Until Sejm (lower house) formally passes the monetary policy outline, we will not publish the reserve money goal," Jacek Osinski, deputy head of the monetary policy department, told Reuters. He did not elaborate.
Reserve money, also called high powered money or monetary base, consists of cash in circulation, cash in vaults and obligatory reserves.
Since January 1996, it has served as the central banks' monetary policy operational target, through which it wants to control money supply growth and consequently inflation.
The Sejm passes each year the central bank's monetary policy plan, submitted together with the budget draft.
